cards.text: Some time later, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, dies, and his son Hanun takes over. Over in Israel, King David wants to be good to the new king.

cards.question: Nahash has died, and his son Hanun is king of the Ammonites now. Why does David want to be good to Hanun?

answers.text: Hanun once helped David in battle
Hanun sent David a gift of silver

cards.text: So David sends messengers to console Hanun about his father. But when they arrive, the Ammonite princes have something to tell Hanun, and friend, they've got a THEORY.

cards.question: The Ammonite princes don't believe David's servants came to comfort Hanun. What do the princes say they really came to do?

answers.text: Spy out the land and overthrow it
Steal the royal treasure for David
Take Hanun back as a prisoner

cards.question: Hanun treats David's servants with honor.

cards.text: Hanun takes David's servants, shaves their beards, cuts off their garments at the hips, and sends them away.

cards.question: Someone tells David what Hanun did to his servants. What does David do?
David's men have been thoroughly humiliated, so he tells them to stay in Jericho. Until when?

answers.text: Until their beards have grown back
Until a full year has passed
Until their new garments are ready

cards.text: Over in Ammon, Hanun and the Ammonites realize they've become a stench to David. Friend, that is NOT a smell a fresh batch can cover up.

cards.question: Hanun and the Ammonites know they've become a stench to David. What do they spend a thousand talents of silver on?

answers.text: A peace gift for King David

cards.text: They hire thirty-two thousand chariots, plus the king of Maacah, who camps near Medeba with his troops while the Ammonites march out for battle. That's not a sorry note, friend, that's a down payment on a WAR.

cards.question: When David hears about this army, he sends Joab, his army commander, with the entire army of mighty men.

cards.text: The Ammonites line up at the entrance to their city, and the kings they hired wait out in the open country. Joab looks around and sees battle lines in front of him AND behind him.

cards.question: Joab has an enemy army in front of him and another behind him. How does he handle it?

answers.text: He splits his troops into two groups
He orders his troops to retreat
He waits for David to come help

cards.question: Facing two armies, Joab picks some of Israel's best men to fight the Arameans himself.

cards.text: The rest of the troops go to Joab's brother Abishai, who lines them up against the Ammonites. Two brothers, two armies, ONE plan.

cards.question: Before the battle, Joab tells his brother Abishai what to do if an enemy is too strong. What does Joab say?

answers.text: If one side is losing the other comes to help
If one side is losing both fall back to Jerusalem
Whichever side wins first gets all the plunder

cards.question: Joab tells Abishai to be strong and fight bravely for their people. How does Joab finish?

answers.text: He leaves the outcome to the LORD
He promises the troops the plunder
He warns the troops not to run

cards.question: Joab and his troops advance to fight the Arameans. What happens?
When the Ammonites see the Arameans run from Joab, they run too.

cards.text: ALL that silver, and the hired help is the first one out the door! The Ammonites run from Abishai into their city, and Joab heads back to Jerusalem.
But the Arameans aren't finished. They send for more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, led by Shophach, the commander of the army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah (1 Chronicles 18:3).

cards.question: When word of the new Aramean army reaches David, he leads all Israel across the Jordan himself.

cards.text: No more sending somebody else. The king himself lines up for battle, and the Arameans fight him.

cards.question: David and the Arameans are locked in battle. How does it end?

answers.text: The Arameans flee and Shophach is killed
The Arameans win and David pulls back
Both armies pull back with no winner

cards.text: David kills seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers.

cards.question: Hadadezer's subjects see that Israel has beaten them. What do they do now?

answers.text: Make peace with David and serve him
Ask the Ammonites for more silver
Pull back and plan another attack

cards.question: After making peace with David, the Arameans are still willing to help the Ammonites.

cards.text: In the spring, the time when kings march out to war, Joab leads out the army. War had a SEASON, friend, right there on the calendar like a dentist appointment.

cards.question: This time, David rides out to war right alongside Joab.
Joab ravages the land of the Ammonites, then besieges their city of Rabbah. How does the siege end?

answers.text: Joab attacks Rabbah and demolishes it
Joab gives up and heads back home
Rabbah holds out and Joab moves on

cards.text: Then David takes the crown right off the head of their king. And friend, this is NOT a crown from a party store.

cards.question: The crown David takes from the Ammonite king is set with precious stones. It weighs a talent of ___.
David takes that heavy crown from the Ammonite king. Where does it end up?

cards.text: A talent of gold on his head, plus a great amount of plunder from the city. Friend, I wear a chef's hat and MY neck gets tired.
David brings out the people who were there and puts them to work with saws, iron picks and axes.

cards.question: David does the same thing in all the other Ammonite cities.

cards.text: Then David and all his troops head home to Jerusalem. Friend, if that army had a group chat, it was nothing but "Leaving now" for an hour straight.
